text:
caroline: FYI Acme reported repeated 400s when using JSON mode for a nested-orders payload. They see 'invalid JSON' and then when they retry they report a billing spike and higher latency.

sam: Can you drop the failing request/response and any client logs? Trying to repro locally.

caroline: Pasting stripped logs + request/response. sensitive fields redacted.
```
REQUEST (client):
POST /v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED, Content-Type: application/json
Body: {
  "json_mode": "strict",
  "orders": [
    {"id": "ord_1001", "amount": 12.5},
    {"id": "ord_1002", "amount": 9.0, "audit": {"received_at": "2025-11-02T14:12:00Z"}}
  ]
}

RESPONSE (server):
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Body: {"error": "invalid_json", "detail": "Unexpected token at position 234"}
x-request-id: req_abc123

Client log (acme):
- got 400, client retried once after refreshing token
- second attempt succeeded but invoice shows 2x tokens billed
```

sam: Interesting — I repro'd with streaming enabled and saw the model sometimes emit a partial closing brace on a separate chunk which our strict parser treats as malformed. When client retries they trigger a fresh generation which gets billed.

leo: Quick note: structured json in streaming can split arrays/objects across chunks. Our parser currently expects the entire JSON object in one contiguous stream. If the model emits: `\n... \"audit\": {\"received_at\": \"2025-...` then newline then `\"\}\"` on next chunk we treat it as stream boundary and fail.

marta: Do we already have a reassembly layer? I thought there was a streaming buffer that reassembles tokens until end-of-stream, but maybe it only applies to text mode, not structured mode.

sam: Repro steps I used (staging):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"json_mode":"strict","stream":true,"orders":[{"id":"ord_1001"},{"id":"ord_1002","amount":9.0,"audit":{"received_at":"2025-11-02T14:12:00Z"}}]}' \n| jq -R -s '.'
```
I hit the 400 reliably when stream chunking was small. Increasing model_chunk_size avoided the parse error.

caroline: Acme is on hosted tier. They asked if there's a config change they can do now.

leo: Short-term workaround: disable streaming or set json_mode to a more tolerant setting if available (e.g., 'json_lines' or 'relaxed'). We shouldn't ask customers to switch off retries; instead tell them to disable client-side automatic retry for 400s from structured-json until we patch.

marta: Long-term fix options: 1) Add a streaming reassembly pass for structured outputs that buffers until a complete JSON token sequence is available, 2) make parser tolerant to boundary-split tokens, or 3) add a server-side canonicalizer that closes dangling braces before parse. Engineering effort varies.

billing-bot: Billing team looped in. Preliminary: we bill on tokens produced by the model, even if final parse fails — failed+retry both consumed tokens. Opened BILL-829 to check whether we can avoid charging for failed parse attempts for hosted customers while we mitigate.

sam: Action items: leo will reproduce and test a reassembly buffer in staging (ETA today), marta will draft parser tolerance plan, billing-bot will confirm billing behavior and communicate any credit flow, caroline to send customer the workaround: disable streaming or turn off automatic retry on 4xx responses and we'll update when we have a fix.

caroline: Thanks — I'll message Acme with the workaround now and ask for request IDs for the failed calls (x-request-id).

leo: Taking lead, tagging @marta if I need deeper parser changes. Will post logs and test results here when done.

marta: ACK, follow up after leo's repro.

billing-bot: BILL-829 created, assigned to billing team.

sam: Also note: customer reported a couple 401s during retries — likely client token refresh behavior. Caroline please check if they are rotating tokens on 401 and then immediately re-sending the same payload which can duplicate charges.

caroline: Will confirm token flow and include in the Acme reply.

leo: quick note: adding tolerant reassembly reduced the 400 rate from ~80% to <5% in my quick tests. Will validate across seed inputs.

caroline: Perfect, keep us posted. :thumbsup:
